summary: Highland sprawls across 18.7 square miles at the base of the San Bernardino Mountains, and from many of its eastern neighborhoods you can look straight up at peaks topping 8,000 feet — a dramatic backdrop that belies the city's otherwise low-slung, quiet-suburban pacing. That mountain proximity is the defining geographic fact: the San Bernardino National Forest begins just minutes from the city's northeastern edge, offering trail access that many Inland Empire cities simply can't match, and the route up Highway 330 toward Big Bear Lake starts practically in Highland's backyard. With a median home value around $455,200 against a median household income near $78,000, the price-to-income ratio lands around 5.8 — more accessible than coastal Southern California but still a meaningful stretch, requiring roughly 23% of gross monthly income just for median rent at $1,539. The city functions largely as a bedroom community; major employment anchors sit in neighboring San Bernardino (healthcare systems, logistics hubs, government offices), and westbound commutes on the 210 freeway are a daily reality. Averaging 9.7 hours of sunshine per day with highs around 73°F, summers run genuinely hot while winters stay mild enough for year-round outdoor use. Highland is a place where mountain access and relative affordability negotiate constantly with limited local employment and a car-dependent street network.
